Batch 87 CYCLE 2 (verification of the final diff) = RULING 106 (b) on the REVIEW path (orchestrator 2026-11-14 '20:21'): "a finished video that passes every gate is always launched and delivered as a candidate; one open integrity point means the REVIEW path with that point in the caption, never left unrendered." With RULING 93 AS AMENDED ('21:10'): a clip whose source-burned captions the 9:16 crop cuts mid-word is 16:9-only. The case (tonight): run pinned_20261115_013448 (Blockware spotlight 3f481f5a): the 16:9 final cleared every one of its 24 gate rows; its 9:16 crop cuts the source's burned captions ('SOLD MY' reads 'D MY'); the run's EDL predates the sealed 'formats' field (absent = both). On re-judgment the builder's L-s step A refused the moment (CONDITION_OUTSIDE, REFERENT_OUTSIDE). telegram.review_drop, an engineering REVIEW to the approval chat (head "REVIEW ONLY - NOT A PASS - not for publishing"; never a release authorisation; texts generated in code, the caller could not edit them), would send BOTH finals and could not state the open point. The change: review_drop(run_dir, send=None, withhold=None, points=()). withhold {format: reason}: formats of this run NOT read or sent, each with a non-empty reason; a format outside the run's formats or a blank reason -> STOP; withholding every format -> STOP. points: caller-stated open integrity points, non-empty strings <= REVIEW_POINT_MAX (300). Only the formats sent are judged (review_nonpass of those formats, unchanged otherwise; the REVIEW_NOT_DROPPABLE rule unchanged for them). review_texts puts "OPEN INTEGRITY POINT:

" and "WITHHELD, NOT SENT: : " lines right under the head of every caption and of the note (the caption is cut from the END by _fit, unchanged); every text then passes the unchanged checks (starts with the head; _review_forbidden: no PASS / PASSED, CANDIDATE FOR APPROVAL, approved, outside the head) AND each stated line must appear WHOLE as a line in every text, else STOP. SIXTEEN_NINE_ONLY ("the package sealed formats ['16x9']") is now printed only when the EDL SEALS 16:9 alone (release_auth.release_formats), never for a caller's withhold. REVIEW_DROP.json records 'withheld' and 'points'. Nothing else changes: no release path, no attestation, no ledger. Tests (test_review_drop, 3 new): the 9:16 withheld (its file deleted first: never read) and a point stated: only the 16:9 is sent, the point and the withheld reason ride whole under the head of the caption and the note, before the 'Not passing' line, recorded in REVIEW_DROP.json, and the 9:16's content-integrity failure (G16 FAIL) does not block the 16:9 drop; MUST-FAIL mirror: without withhold both finals go and no point line exists; refusals, nothing sent and no REVIEW_DROP.json: an unknown format, a blank reason, every format withheld, an empty / too long / non-string point, a point with 'passed', four 300-character points that cannot fit whole in a 1024-character caption. 25 + 24 (delivery) pass; on the old code (c396c3c8) the 3 new tests fail. Cycle 1 (qwen27b PASS 0.85, glm PASS 0.85, no consensus): glm's low note (a withheld reason had no length cap; it failed closed via the whole-line check) is closed: a withheld reason is now capped at REVIEW_POINT_MAX like a point, with a refusal test. FIND: a way for a caller to make the drop look like a pass, a release or an approval; a withheld format still read or sent; a stated point cut, dropped or hidden from any caption; a content-integrity failure of a SENT format that no longer blocks; any change for a caller that passes neither withhold nor points. Only state what you can verify from the diff. Reply with the JSON verdict; keep the reasoning short; at most 3 findings.

consensus_findings.issue: The withheld-reason line is built with fmt.replace('x',':') so a caller-supplied reason containing the literal '9:16' vs '9x16' mismatch is cosmetic only, but more importantly the withheld dict is passed to review_texts as (withhold or {}).items() while review_drop already normalised it; if a caller passes a non-dict truthy withhold (e.g. a list of pairs) review_drop's dict() would raise before the friendly STOP, yet the friendly message claims formats outside the run — minor, fails closed.
consensus_findings.evidence: withhold, points = dict(withhold or {}), list(points or ())

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: A withheld reason containing a newline (or a point with '\n') passes the <=300/strip checks but breaks the whole-line guarantee: the stated line is split across lines, so set(need) <= set(t.split('\n')) fails and the drop refuses — or, if the caller's reason's last segment matches, the recorded 'withheld'/'points' in REVIEW_DROP.json no longer match what a reader sees as one line.
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.evidence:
need = [REVIEW_POINT_HEAD + p for p in points] + [f"{WITHHELD_HEAD}{f.replace('x',':')}: {r}" ...]; check is set(need) <= set(t.split("
")) — a reason like 'a
b' makes the joined line 'WITHHELD, NOT SENT: 9:16: a
b' which never appears as a single line, so review_drop raises 'does not fit whole' even though it fits by length; the friendly error misleads and no test covers embedded newlines.
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: Either reject/strip newlines in reasons and points (r.strip() -> r.replace('\n',' ').strip() or a regex check) or, in the whole-line check, compare against the reconstructed multi-line expectation; add a test with a reason containing '\n'.
